record.summary: White House recommendations to Congress for a national AI policy framework, in seven parts. Congress should preempt unduly burdensome state AI laws and bar states from regulating AI development, while keeping states' general laws protecting children, preventing fraud and protecting consumers, their zoning of AI infrastructure and their own AI use. It proposes age assurance, parental tools and safeguards against sexual exploitation and self-harm on AI services likely used by minors, a federal framework against unauthorised AI digital replicas, and enough capacity in national security agencies to understand frontier model capabilities. It opposes a new federal AI rulemaking body.
record.notes: Released on 20 March 2026; the document itself is dated March 2026. The White House release of that day describes six key objectives and adds that the framework can succeed only if applied uniformly across the country, the subject of the document's seventh part on preempting state AI laws. Section 8 of EO 14365 (US-20) had called for a legislative recommendation preempting conflicting state AI laws, with carve-outs for child safety, AI compute and data centre infrastructure, and state procurement and use of AI. The recommendations ask Congress to build on the TAKE IT DOWN Act (US-14). The FTC's proposed policy statement of 1 July 2026 (US-24) cites the framework. The White House fact sheet on EO 14434 of 29 September 2026 (US-26) calls it a 'National Super Intelligence Policy Framework with legislative recommendations', following that order's renaming of AI as 'Super Intelligence'.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the whitehouse.gov PDF stored on 11 Oct 2026 (the archiver found it unchanged on 17 Oct 2026). It confirms the title, 'MARCH 2026', the seven sections and the recommendations in the summary. The PDF gives only the month; the day, 20 March 2026, rests on the White House release of that day, stored in this run, so date_published stays 2026-03-20. The White House fact sheet of 29 Sep 2026, also stored in this run, supports the notes and the current status. The earlier summary called the document recommendations 'under EO 14365 Sec. 8', which the document does not say, and said it 'creates no dedicated frontier-model regulatory regime', an inference; both were replaced with what the text says. The earlier notes rested the date on law-firm summaries.

judgment.status_reasoning: A set of non-binding recommendations to Congress, released 20 March 2026; the release says the Administration looks forward to working with Congress to turn it into legislation. Nothing stored withdraws it; the White House fact sheet of 29 Sep 2026, stored in this run, refers to it as the framework the White House unveiled. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: The administration's legislative framework for AI, with child-safety, frontier-capability and preemption content; in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: Cover: 'MARCH 2026'. The White House release dated 20 March 2026 says the Administration is issuing the framework 'today'. date_published 2026-03-20 is therefore confirmed from an official source.
